01what it is

A fork of FlClash on the mihomo core.

Routing runs on the same mihomo core as Clash.Meta. ReClash adds what was missing on top: provider theming and widgets, smart routing, a built-in DPI bypass, and a dashboard rebuilt from scratch.

open sourcemihomo core

The project is not affiliated with FlClash, mihomo or FlClashX. How it differs from FlClash.

lineage

  • mihomothe routing core: rules, groups, GeoIP, fake-ip
  • FlClashthe cross-platform Flutter base
  • ReClashprovider themes, smart routing, DPI bypass, a dashboard rebuilt
02what it does

What ReClash does.

01

The full mihomo core

Rules, groups, proxy providers, GeoIP and GeoSite, fake-ip, external controllers — everything you expect from Clash.Meta.

02

Smart routing

The “Auto” mode keeps a working node for the current network and switches when the network changes — starting from a region preset.

How “Auto” works
03

The look comes from the provider

A single response header repaints the app in your brand: colour, background, connection ring, logo and the widget set.

See how it works
04

A dashboard of widgets

Fifteen widgets: speed, traffic usage, mode, network detection, TUN, system proxy, announcement, service card.

05

Whole device or just apps

TUN mode captures the whole system; the system proxy covers only the apps that support it. Switch it from the main screen.

06

Traffic and expiry, at a glance

The client reads your remaining traffic and expiry straight from the subscription and keeps them on the main screen — no dashboard visit needed.

03for users

Setup is one link and three steps.

The subscription is yours to bring — everything you have to do is below.

no accountimport by link

  1. 01

    Install the client

    Windows, macOS, Linux or Android. Installer or portable build — no account, no sign-up, no email.

  2. 02

    Add the subscription with one link

    The link from your provider brings the profile, the servers and the rules in one go. Nothing to fill in by hand.

  3. 03

    Connect

    Choose TUN for the whole device or system proxy for apps that support it. You can switch the mode from the main screen at any time.

the import link

Already have a subscription link?

Paste it here and get a link that opens ReClash and imports the profile in one tap. A provider can put the very same button in their dashboard.

The finished import linkreclash://install-config?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsub.example%2Flink%2Fabc123

That is a sample. Paste your own link and we will build yours.

The link is assembled in your browser and never leaves it.

Download ReClashQuick start
04for providers

Your app. You just don't build it.

No SDK, no plugin, no agreement. Add a few HTTP headers to the subscription response and the user's client shows your logo, your colour, your remaining traffic and your renewal button.

Open the docsBuild the headers

The builder emits ready-made artefacts for the Remnawave panel; next to it are mock subscriptions to test against.

ReClash
Profile imported from a link.
Traffic62 / 200 GB
Amsterdam · 24 ms

The headers configure the whole look of the client — service name, colour and palette, hero ring and effect, widget set, announcement, renew buttons, fallback hosts and more. 19 reclash-* headers in all; the client also reads standard subscription headers and understands a subset of FlClashX names as aliases — the full reference.

05platforms

Runs on four platforms.

Windows
  • Windows 10 and newer
  • installer and portable build
  • TUN and system proxy
macOS
  • Intel and Apple Silicon
  • DMG image
  • TUN via the system helper
Linux
  • AppImage, deb, rpm
  • x86_64 · arm64
  • TUN and system proxy
Android
  • Android 6 and newer
  • per-ABI APKs
  • VPN service mode

Current files are always on the downloads page.

06the honest bit

Leave whenever you want.

No account, no lock-in. Your servers and profiles are yours, and a subscription in the plain Clash format moves to any compatible client. ReClash is fully open and sells nothing — there is no paid “access” here that could ever be taken away.
